euronews.description: The temporary suspension of the Schengen agreement was prompted by concerns over the migrant crisis in Ceuta.

euronews.title: Sovereignty, sarcasm, blame: How North Africa reacted to Ceuta crisis
euronews.description: Morocco's press framed Ceuta as a sovereignty question, Algerian media accused Rabat of "weaponising" migration, and Tunisian social media responded with dark humour, as the region's own economic and political crises remained in the background.

euronews.title: Ancient mummy DNA in Chile shows that colonisation brought smallpox to the Americas
euronews.description: Analysis of DNA from Chilean mummies has revealed the earliest known genome of the smallpox virus recovered from the Americas.

euronews.title: Barack Obama pays tribute to Irish musician Glen Hansard in his summer 2026 playlist
euronews.description: Barack Obama continues his longstanding tradition of sharing his music (and literature) picks for the summer - and has paid tribute to the Oscar-winning Irish musician Glen Hansard, who tragically died this week in a motorcycle crash at the age of 56.

euronews.description: Cosplayers in elaborate costumes gather at ChinaJoy in Shanghai, where gaming fans meet characters inspired by popular video games.

euronews.title: Miss Supranational: The young pretender challenging the old guards in beauty pageant
euronews.description: Held in southern Poland, Miss Supranational is a beauty pageant you may never have heard of -- but it has quietly grown into one of the world's leading competitions, challenging the dominance of Miss Universe and Miss World.

euronews.title: More than 48,000 migrants return to Morocco after mass crossing into Ceuta
euronews.description: Some 48,000 of the roughly 50,000 people who crossed illegally into Ceuta since early Friday have already been returned to Morocco, as Madrid condemned the mass crossing as an "attack" on its sovereignty.

euronews.title: EU considers emergency meeting as nuclear shutdown leaves Hungary facing energy crisis
euronews.description: Hungarian PM Péter Magyar has warned of an energy crisis after record-low Danube water levels forced the shutdown of the Paks nuclear plant, which supplies nearly half the country's power.

euronews.title: Volcanic land with cold doubts: Iceland decides on EU negotiations amidst hopes and fears
euronews.description: On August 29 Iceland is voting by referendum whether or not to resume EU membership negotiations, suspended since 2013. We travelled to the volcanic island to investigate the pros and cons, fears, hopes, expectations and doubts - and discovered a hotly polarised society.

euronews.title: A history of own goals: Gianni Infantino's timeline of FIFA controversies
euronews.description: Europe's national teams have threatened to boycott the FIFA World Cup if Gianni Infantino pushes ahead with his controversial plan to privatise the tournament. Euronews Culture looks back at what brought the world of football under FIFA to breaking point.

euronews.title: Cyprus: 44-year-old accused of spying on British base for Iran
euronews.description: The man, a dual British and Azerbaijani national, is being held in Cyprus while extradition proceedings are underway. It is the first British investigation abroad under the National Security Act.

rfi.title: 'Humanitarian emergency' as influx of migrants overwhelms Spanish enclave Ceuta
rfi.description: Some 60,000 migrants entered Spain’s north African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco in the space of 24 hours, between Thursday and Friday, leaving at least 34 dead and prompting France to tighten controls along its border with Spain.

rfi.title: As Bordeaux blaze eases, Ukraine sends reinforcements to France
rfi.description: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday that 308 people have been detained nationwide over the wildfire outbreak, with two-thirds suspected of "deliberate arson". The announcement came as the blaze near Bordeaux showed signs of easing and Ukraine dispatched 70 rescuers to help battle the fires still burning across France.

rfi.title: Fifa chiefs criticise media for 'misreporting' World Cup sell-off plans
rfi.description: Executives at world football's governing body Fifa on Friday said "incorrect" media reports had "disrupted" the presentation of its proposals to open up the World Cup to outside investors.

rfi.title: France freezes assets of controversial Russian commentator Fedorova
rfi.description: France has frozen the assets of pro-Kremlin commentator Xenia Fedorova for six months, the government announced on Friday, adding a financial measure to an expulsion order already issued against her over accusations of spreading Kremlin propaganda on French television and undermining democracy.

rfi.title: Where you live could decide how well you breathe, French study finds
rfi.description: Repeated heatwaves in France are taking a toll on people's lungs, doctors say, with young patients with no prior respiratory issues increasingly being admitted to hospital, a leading pulmonologist has told RFI.

rfi.title: Russia seeks arrest of Telegram's Durov over 'terrorism complicity' claims
rfi.description: Russia has announced it is seeking the arrest of Telegram founder Pavel Durov over accusations of "complicity in terrorism", alleging he allowed the platform to be used for recruitment by Ukraine's security services.

rfi.title: EU crisis chief calls for prevention funding as wildfire crisis rages on
rfi.description: As firefighters continue to battle major blazes in France, the European Union's crisis management chief is calling for more investment in prevention, forest management and emergency response.

rfi.title: DRC court clears path to change a constitution that says it can't be changed
rfi.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Constitutional Court has approved a referendum law that critics say could pave the way for President Felix Tshisekedi to seek a third term in office, prompting a coalition of opposition parties to reject the ruling and vow to fight the change.

rfi.title: Migrant exodus leaves South African employers short-handed
rfi.description: South Africa is suffering a drop in its workforce, following the departure of thousands of foreign workers in the wake of a wave of xenophobic attacks, anti-migrant protests and intensified immigration enforcement.

rfi.title: EU condemns Iranian 'aggression' against French diplomats
rfi.description: The European Union on Tuesday condemned an "aggression" this month by Iranian security services against two French diplomats in Tehran.

rfi.title: Zelensky hails ‘good meeting’ with Trump as Ukraine seeks Patriot missile deal
rfi.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has hailed a “good meeting” with United States President Donald Trump at the White House, saying the two leaders discussed plans to produce Patriot air-defence interceptors and ways to revive stalled negotiations with Russia.

rfi.title: Renault to face criminal trial in France over 'dieselgate' emissions scandal
rfi.description: Renault will face a criminal trial in France on aggravated fraud charges over accusations that devices in its diesel cars were designed to cheat clean air laws, the public prosecutor's office told French news agency AFP.

rfi.title: Rift deepens as US walks out of UN over French criticism of Trump
rfi.description: United States diplomats walked out of a United Nations Security Council meeting on Monday as their French counterparts were speaking, after Paris criticised the Trump administration’s human rights record and backed a second term for human rights chief Volker Turk. The move underlined the growing strain in relations between Washington and one of its closest European allies.

rfi.title: Family of missing French tourist demands Japan's national police take over case
rfi.description: A statue honouring Tiphaine Véron, the French tourist who vanished in Japan in 2018, was unveiled on Wednesday near the hotel where she was last seen. Eight years on and still without any solid leads, her family is now pushing for Japan's national police to take over the stalled investigation.

rfi.title: France legend Zidane succeeds Deschamps as boss of Les Bleus
rfi.description: Zinédine Zidane was officially appointed as France's new head coach on Tuesday, succeeding Didier Deschamps, the French Football Federation announced.

rfi.title: US reviews troop presence in Europe as Washington pushes NATO burden sharing
rfi.description: The United States began reviewing its military presence in Europe on Monday, officials said, after US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth told his NATO counterparts last month that Washington was planning such an analysis.

rfi.title: Uganda health minister declares end to latest Ebola outbreak
rfi.description: Uganda's health minister on Tuesday declared the country Ebola-free, following the latest outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic disease which infected 20 people and killed two in the country.

rfi.title: UK's Burnham pledges new drone tech to Ukraine in Zelensky meeting
rfi.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged new drone-jamming technology to Ukraine on Monday, using his first meeting with a foreign leader since taking office to underline Britain's continued military backing for Kyiv.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Ceuta : plus de 48 000 personnes sont déjà rentrées au Maroc, annonce le gouvernement espagnol ; face aux critiques, Pedro Sanchez appelle à l’unité des Européens
lemonde.description: Le ministère de l’intérieur espagnol avait annoncé plus tôt dans la journée que 50 000 personnes avaient afflué dans l’enclave depuis jeudi. Selon le quotidien « El Pais », 57 migrants sont morts en tentant de rejoindre le territoire à la nage.

lemonde.title: Incendie en Gironde : Sophie Brocas, préfète, et Marc Vermeulen, patron des pompiers du département, racontent dix jours de lutte contre le feu et expliquent leurs choix
lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », la préfète de Gironde et le directeur du Service départemental d’incendie et de secours reviennent sur leur gestion du mégafeu qui sévit dans le département depuis le 22 juillet.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Donald Trump dit vouloir faire « très attention » avant d’autoriser Kiev à produire des missiles Patriot
lemonde.description: « Vous donnez cette technologie et, un jour, ils peuvent se retourner contre vous », a mis en garde le président américain, lors d’un conseil des ministres ouvert à la presse dans sa résidence de Camp David. Le président américain avait annoncé, le 8 juillet, son intention d’autoriser l’Ukraine à fabriquer des missiles Patriot, à l’issue du sommet de l’Organisation du traité de l’Atlantique Nord à Ankara.

lemonde.title: « Ce que vivent les Palestiniens en Cisjordanie occupée dépasse la violence ordinaire et correspond exactement à la définition du terrorisme »
lemonde.description: Arie Perliger, professeur à l’université du Massachusetts à Lowell, spécialiste du terrorisme d’extrême droite en Israël et aux Etats-Unis, revient dans un entretien au « Monde » sur les ressorts idéologiques de la violence des colons en Cisjordanie occupée et sur les responsabilités du gouvernement israélien dans sa persistance.

lemonde.title: Au Pakistan, sur les pentes du Broad Peak, les difficiles recherches pour retrouver les 10 alpinistes ensevelis, dont Nirmal Purja
lemonde.description: Dix personnes ont été prises dans une avalanche, jeudi, dans la chaîne du Karakoram. Parmi elles, l’alpiniste népalais connu pour avoir gravi les 14 plus hauts sommets du monde en un temps record. Quatre corps ont été repérés. Les recherches reprendront samedi.

lemonde.title: En Serbie, la série « Opération Sabre » ravive les fantômes du passé
lemonde.description: « Tour du monde en séries » (5/6). En retraçant l’assassinat du premier ministre Zoran Djindjic et l’enquête qui a suivi, la série serbe a attiré 1 million de spectateurs chaque semaine et ranimé les débats sur la corruption, le nationalisme et l’héritage des années Milosevic.

lemonde.title: El Niño, qui se renforce, « attise une planète déjà en feu », s’alarme le chef de l’ONU
lemonde.description: Ce phénomène naturel revient tous les deux à sept ans. Les eaux de surface dans le centre et l’est de l’océan Pacifique équatorial se réchauffent, ce qui entraîne pendant plusieurs mois des modifications majeures des régimes de vent, de pression et de précipitations à l’échelle mondiale.

lemonde.title: Un responsable de la FNSEA présente ses excuses à Marine Tondelier, après l’avoir insultée
lemonde.description: Ce responsable agricole de l’Oise l’avait traitée de « grosse salope » sur sa page privée après l’adoption de la loi d’urgence agricole. La candidate écologiste avait exigé des excuses, menaçant le responsable syndical de « poursuites judiciaires ».

lemonde.title: Les journalistes de « Marianne » affirment que Jean Quatremer pourrait « tordre » l’ADN du magazine et « brusquer » ses lecteurs
lemonde.description: La directrice de la rédaction, Eve Szeftel, a cependant assuré que Jean Quatremer, qui vient de quitter le journal « Libération », « ne va exercer aucun rôle dans la direction de la rédaction, ni l’orientation du journal », mais « va exprimer une opinion ».

lemonde.title: Surpopulation carcérale : au 1ᵉʳ juillet, le nombre de détenus dans les prisons françaises atteint 89 446, un nouveau record
lemonde.description: Le taux de sur-occupation dans les prisons et les maisons d’arrêt, où sont détenues les personnes condamnées à de courtes peines ou celles en attente de jugement, était de 141,3 % au 1ᵉʳ juillet.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : le trafic maritime est toujours impossible dans le détroit d’Ormuz, affirme l’Iran
lemonde.description: « En raison de la persistance des actes agressifs des forces militaires des Etats-Unis dans la région, le passage par le détroit d’Ormuz n’est pas possible », déclare l’Autorité du détroit du golfe Persique, mise sur pied par Téhéran pour contrôler le trafic.

lemonde.title: La mère des cinq bébés morts découverts à Orange a été mise en examen et placée en détention provisoire
lemonde.description: Les ossements de quatre nourrissons et le corps d’un nouveau-né ont été retrouvés dans un appartement d’Orange (Vaucluse), au domicile d’une famille dont la femme a accouché dimanche d’un bébé en bonne santé.

lemonde.title: Quand le gouvernement américain publie une carte fantaisiste de l’Afrique
lemonde.description: Lors d’une conférence internationale sur le sida, au Brésil, fin juillet, le département d’Etat a présenté une carte de l’Afrique où la Côte d’Ivoire s’est retrouvée dans le sud du continent et le Nigeria enclavé dans le Sahara. Le Cameroun, quant à lui, est devenu un Etat fantôme.

lemonde.title: Où acheter en France pour bénéficier d’une vie culturelle riche ?
lemonde.description: « Nouveau logis, nouvelle vie » (3/6). Visiter des expositions et des monuments historiques ou assister à des concerts est important pour de nombreux Français. Cela peut même devenir un critère lorsqu’il s’agit de choisir un lieu de vie.

lemonde.title: En Nouvelle-Calédonie, un nouveau président de gouvernement sans majorité et avec des défis majeurs
lemonde.description: A 41 ans, le président de l’Eveil océanien, Milakulo Tukumuli, a été désigné vendredi président du gouvernement collégial de l’archipel. Mais son élection, fruit d’un accord avec les non-indépendantistes, ne lui garantit pas de faire passer les réformes qu’il a promis de mener.

lemonde.title: La FIFA entend poursuivre son plan d’ouverture aux investisseurs privés ; un conseiller de Gianni Infantino démissionne en signe de protestation
lemonde.description: « Personne n’est en train de vendre le football », se défend l’instance internationale, alors que l’UEFA a annoncé qu’elle boycotterait les futures compétitions, dont les Coupes du monde, si le projet n’était pas abandonné. Vendredi, Carlos Cordeiro, proche conseiller de Gianni Infantino, a quitté son poste.

france24fr.title: Rumeurs, appel d'air, passivité du Maroc... comment expliquer l'afflux inédit de migrants à Ceuta ?
france24fr.description: Plusieurs hypothèses sont évoquées pour expliquer l'afflux soudain de 60 000 migrants à la frontière de l'enclave espagnole de Ceuta au Maroc. Si l'extrême droite européenne estime que la politique migratoire de Pedro Sanchez a créé un appel d'air, plusieurs témoignages rapportent des rumeurs d'ouverture d'un poste frontière ayant conduit à cette crise. La presse espagnole s'interroge également sur le rôle des autorités marocaines.

france24fr.title: Non, cette vidéo ne montre pas l'attaque de drones contre des navires en Égypte
france24fr.description: Après l'annonce d'une attaque de drone contre un navire de stockage de gaz lié à des intérêts américains en Égypte, une vidéo présentée comme montrant l'incident a circulé en ligne. Mais ces images sont trompeuses : France 24 a établi qu'elles montrent en réalité un drone ukrainien frappant un navire russe en mer Noire.

france24fr.title: Ceuta : Trump dénonce une "invasion" au moment où la majorité des migrants rentrent au Maroc
france24fr.description: Donald Trump et l'extrême droite européenne ont utilisé les images de Ceuta, jeudi et vendredi, pour défendre leur politique anti-immigration et attaquer leurs adversaires de gauche. Dans le même temps, plus de 48 000 des 60 000 migrants arrivés dans l'enclave espagnole sont déjà retournés au Maroc en moins d'une journée, selon le ministère espagnol de l'Intérieur.

france24fr.title: En RDC, la validation de la loi référendaire ravive les tensions politiques
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, la validation d'une loi référendaire qui relance le débat sur un possible 3e mandat de Félix Tshisekedi ravive les tensions politiques. L'opposition dénonce une remise en cause de la Constitution et appelle à la mobilisation.

france24fr.title: Incendies en Gironde : 160 000 personnes autorisées à regagner leur domicile
france24fr.description: Face à la menace du mégafeu, désormais "contenu", des milliers de personnes évacuées sont invitées à revenir chez elles, tandis que certaines restent dans l’attente. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Crise migratoire à Ceuta : l’Europe en alerte après l’arrivée massive de migrants
france24fr.description: L'arrivée massive de migrants à Ceuta met les Européens en alerte. Alors qu'Emmanuel Macron demande à son ministre de l'Intérieur de renforcer les contrôles à la frontière avec l'Espagne, l'Italie souhaite suspendre Madrid de l'espace Schengen. En retour, le gouvernement espagnol a convoqué l'ambassadeur de l'Italie. Récit de Nicolas Chamontin.

france24fr.title: L’identité du Figaro usurpée pour une fausse citation de Jean-Noël Barrot sur Xenia Fedorova
france24fr.description: Un visuel du Figaro a été détourné pour attribuer au ministre des Affaires étrangères français, Jean-Noël Barrot, des propos qu'il n'a jamais prononcés sur l'expulsion de l'ancienne dirigeante de RT France, Xenia Fedorova.

france24fr.title: Ceuta : Pedro Sanchez réagit après l'arrivée massive de migrants
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre espagnol Pedro Sanchez a qualifié vendredi d'"attaque", de "violation de l'intégrité territoriale de l'Espagne" l'arrivée massive de quelque 60 000 migrants dans l'enclave de Ceuta depuis le Maroc. Il a estimé que cette crise migratoire en cours était liée à une interprétation malhonnête "par les mafias" d'une récente décision de justice statuant sur la reconduite des migrants arrivés par la mer.

france24fr.title: Incendies en Grèce : ordre d'évacuation près d'Athènes, la Crète en proie aux flammes
france24fr.description: La Protection civile grecque a ordonné vendredi l'évacuation préventive d'une partie d'une banlieue à l'ouest d'Athènes en raison d'un incendie de forêt, selon un message d'alerte envoyé sur les téléphones portables. Par ailleurs, l'île touristique de Crète était toujours la proie des flammes, poussées par des vents violents malgré une certaine amélioration, selon les pompiers.

france24fr.title: Incendies en Gironde : deux-cent-trente soldats du feu blessés dans les incendies
france24fr.description: Après neuf jours de lutte acharnée contre un mégafeu qui a dévasté 42 000 hectares de forêt en Gironde, les pompiers sont éprouvés par la fatigue et leur santé est affectée par la fumée. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Crise migratoire à Ceuta : 60 000 migrants ont passé la frontière
france24fr.description: Soixante mille migrants ont rejoint l'enclave espagnole de Ceuta au Maroc en quelques jours, provoquant une crise diplomatique européenne quant à la potentielle suspension de l'Espagne de l'espace Schengen. Correspondance de Pierre Benazet depuis Bruxelles pour France 24.

france24fr.title: Cap-Vert : Ceuzany Pires signe un dernier album dédié aux violences domestiques
france24fr.description: Direction le Cap-Vert à la rencontre de Ceuzany Pires, l’une des voix les plus prometteuses de l’archipel. Comparée à la légendaire Cesária Évora, elle rêve aujourd’hui de faire rayonner la musique cap-verdienne à l’international. Son quatrième album porte également une blessure intime et un message fort : victime de violences conjugales, elle transforme son traumatisme en un puissant outil de sensibilisation. Récit d'Awa Diouf.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : le départ de Pape Thiaw bloqué par l'État
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, le feuilleton est loin d’avoir connu son épilogue dans l’affaire opposant Pape Thiaw à la Fédération sénégalaise de football. Alors qu’il a été limogé par la FSF, le ministère des Sports, chargé du paiement du salaire du sélectionneur des Lions de la Teranga, refuse de verser les indemnités de licenciement de Pape Thiaw, invoquant des raisons juridiques. Correspondance d'Elimane Ndao depuis Dakar pour France 24.

france24fr.title: Sanchez dénonce une rumeur lancée par des "mafias de trafiquants d'êtres humains"
france24fr.description: Soixante mille migrants ont rejoint l'enclave espagnole de Ceuta au Maroc en quelques jours, provoquant une crise diplomatique européenne quant à la potentielle suspension de l'Espagne de l'espace Schengen.

france24fr.title: Tous les six mois, cet îlot passe de la France à l'Espagne... et inversement
france24fr.description: Depuis plus d'un siècle, la France et l'Espagne se partagent l'administration de l'île des Faisans, un petit bout de terre posé au milieu de la Bidassoa. Du 1er août au 31 janvier, le plus petit condominium au monde est français, et le reste du temps, il est espagnol !

france24fr.title: Des zones d'ombre persistent après l'explosion de la distillerie Montebello en Guadeloupe
france24fr.description: Une semaine après l’explosion meurtrière de la distillerie Montebello en Guadeloupe, des zones d'ombre persistent. Le bilan est de deux morts et l'enquête se poursuit. Entre un rapport alertant sur des anomalies avant le drame et la polémique autour d'une cagnotte lancée par l’entreprise, les familles et les syndicats réclament des réponses. Le récit de Nicolas Suire avec nos équipes sur place.

france24fr.title: Crise à Ceuta : peut-on exclure l'Espagne de l'espace Schengen comme le réclame Giorgia Meloni ?
france24fr.description: L'Italie a dit jeudi vouloir fermer l'espace Schengen à l'Espagne après que des milliers de migrants sont entrés illégalement ces derniers jours dans l'enclave espagnole de Ceuta en provenance du Maroc. Problème : aucun texte ne prévoit d'exclure un pays membre de la zone de libre circulation de l'Union européenne.

france24fr.title: Ouverture de la Fifa aux investisseurs privés : le projet qui fracture le football mondial
france24fr.description: Boycott de l'UEFA, rejet de plusieurs confédérations, plainte pour corruption et démission d'un proche conseiller de Gianni Infantino : le projet Fifa Forward Enterprise, censé révolutionner le financement du football mondial, plonge la Fifa dans l'une des plus graves crises de son histoire récente. Mais en quoi consiste réellement ce projet ?

spiegel.description: Neue Regeln für den kleinsten Staat der Welt: Leo XIV. legt ein neues Grundgesetz für den Vatikan vor. Gestärkt wird die Präsidentin.

spiegel.description: Die Hamas gibt die Waffen ab, Israels Armee zieht sich zurück, dann beginnt der Wiederaufbau – soweit der Plan des US-Präsidenten. Für Israels Premier Benjamin Netanyahu kommt die jüngste Initiative zur Unzeit.

spiegel.title: Ceuta: Darum wollen so viele Menschen aus Marokko nach Spanien
spiegel.description: Zehntausende sind aus Marokko in die spanische Exklave Ceuta gelangt – innerhalb weniger Tage. Was sind die Gründe für die Massenflucht? Marokkos König preist seine Erfolge, junge Menschen sehen das anders.

spiegel.title: Fifa-Investorenpläne: Auch Kevin Lamour wendet sich gegen Gianni Infantino
spiegel.description: Es könne sein, dass er nun seinen Job verliere, aber dann könne er zumindest »nachts ruhig schlafen«: Kevin Lamour, ein hoher Fifa-Funktionär aus Infantinos Umfeld, kritisiert dessen Vorgehen. Niemand sei in den WM-Plan eingeweiht gewesen.

spiegel.title: Dunja Hayali und ihre Bahn-Kritik: Was stimmt mit dieser ZDF-Doku nicht?

La Néerlandaise de l’équipe FDJ United-Suez brigue le maillot jaune dans la course qui s’élance de Lausanne le 1er août. Installée au bord du lac des Quatre-Cantons, elle se dit inspirée par ce qu’elle nomme «le style de vie à la suisse»

observador.description: Alberto Gonçalves comenta a situação caótica que se está a viver em Ceuta, com 60 mil imigrantes a entrar clandestinamente em Espanha, e alerta para os riscos de alastramento para a Europa.

observador.description: Os abusos ocorreram em Portalegre e Queluz, em 2025. O ADN do feto — resultante de gravidez entretanto interrompida — confirmou a paternidade.

observador.description: Tânger Corrêa (CH) diz que portugueses e espanhóis não seriam afetados pelo fecho das fronteiras. Catarina Martins (BE) considera a proposta inútil, por já haver fiscalização à saída de Ceuta.

observador.title: "Asas" de Ana Rocha de Sousa vai a Odessa

observador.title: Eclipse total: Rio de Onor cancelado, aeródromo avança
observador.description: As atividades referentes ao eclipse solar do próximo dia 12 de agosto foram canceladas em Rio de Onor e Guadramil, no concelho de Bragança. Programação foi deslocada para o aeródromo municipal.

observador.title: Pai de atirador em escola condenado a 15 anos de prisão

phys-org.description: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted severe consequences of unchecked respiratory disease, including cytokine storms. This phenomenon affected many COVID-19 patients and is a potential side effect of many other diseases involving significant inflammation, but approaches to treating these symptoms remain unclear.

phys-org.title: Diego Rivera claimed his mural Creation was half wax, but chemical forensics says otherwise
phys-org.description: Adorning the walls of San Ildefonso College in Mexico City is artist Diego Rivera's masterpiece, rendered in fresco and gold leaf, The Creation, or La Creacioń. It depicts a man standing with his arms outstretched beneath a deep blue celestial disk studded with stars and constellations, while figures seated on clouds watch from either side. The work catalyzed the revival of the encaustic painting technique in the 1920s.

phys-org.title: New low-water method could make production of clean-energy materials much greener
phys-org.description: A new Concordia study has demonstrated a greener way to produce an important class of catalytic materials with promising potential for cleaner energy technologies that rely more on acoustic energy than water and chemicals. The work is published in the journal Advanced Synthesis & Catalysis.

phys-org.title: Magnetic nanoparticles remove forever chemicals from water
phys-org.description: PFAS, otherwise known as forever chemicals, have become commonplace in numerous everyday and industrial products. At the same time, they are some of the most problematic pollutants of our times: They are extremely durable, accumulate in the environment and in organisms and can only be removed from water with difficulty.

phys-org.title: French, Italian winegrowers face earliest ever harvest
phys-org.description: Scorching summer temperatures have disrupted life for millions of Europeans, but for winegrowers in Italy and France who are harvesting their grapes unusually early, the hot weather offers pros as well as cons.

phys-org.title: A discarded SpaceX rocket is on a high-speed collision course with the moon
phys-org.description: A drifting SpaceX rocket is on a collision course with the moon after launching a pair of lunar landers more than a year ago.

phys-org.title: Ancient Irish volcano offers new clues about the development of its modern-day, active 'brothers and sisters'
phys-org.description: An international team of volcanologists working on Carlingford Mountain has found that liquid "magma chambers" do not always exist beneath volcanoes. The team instead demonstrated that magma "plumbing systems" beneath Earth's surface can fluctuate between solid- and liquid-dominated states, providing an improved view of how active volcanoes evolve through time.

phys-org.title: Agricultural waste could fuel protein-rich black soldier fly larvae for human foods
phys-org.description: They're wriggly black grubs more commonly tossed to backyard hens than served at the dinner table, but black soldier fly larvae could soon play a key role in building a more sustainable food system, according to new research from Adelaide University.

phys-org.title: Only 1 in 3 people arrested by ICE have a criminal conviction, research reveals
phys-org.description: Just 34% of people arrested by the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents during President Donald Trump's second term have a criminal conviction, according to research published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. That's a near-historic low, the authors note.

phys-org.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 4961-4967: Approaching a break in the rock record?
phys-org.description: Curiosity spent the week continuing to climb her way through the layers of Mount Sharp, exploring the sedimentary rock strip chart of Martian history. The rover has reached a layer where the science team had spotted a possible "erosional supersurface" by analyzing orbital data alongside images of the layers in the buttes above us.

phys-org.title: Ancient Rome's food shortages were shaped more by logistics than climate
phys-org.description: Ancient Rome's greatest threat to food security wasn't the weather but the challenge of getting grain to the capital, according to a new study. By comparing hundreds of years of historical records with reconstructions of past climate, researchers found that periods of unusual heat, cold, drought or heavy rainfall rarely lined up with reported food shortages.

phys-org.title: Japan probe made closest-ever asteroid flyby: space agency
phys-org.description: A Japanese probe flew 400 meters (1,312 feet) from a near-Earth asteroid this month, marking the closest approach ever recorded for such a mission, the space agency said.

phys-org.title: Consumer confidence rises for second straight month; views remain downbeat amid high prices
phys-org.description: Consumer sentiment confirmed its early-July reading, landing almost 12% above June, according to the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers.

phys-org.title: New method flags hurricane rapid intensification up to five days ahead
phys-org.description: The rapid intensification of a hurricane ranks among the most dangerous weather events on Earth. Storms such as Hurricane Michael, which crashed ashore in the Florida Panhandle with winds of 160 mph (about 257 km/h), and Hurricane Otis, the costliest hurricane to strike Mexico's Pacific coast, caught communities unawares when they intensified at a rate that computer models failed to anticipate.

phys-org.title: Diamond's newfound defect may tame vibrations that hinder quantum light sources
phys-org.description: Researchers in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign have discovered a new type of quantum light emitter in diamonds that could help overcome a number of challenges facing quantum technologies.

phys-org.title: Newsom reverses on long-sought paid leave benefit for California teachers
phys-org.description: The majority of California's roughly 300,000 teachers don't have access to the state-funded paid leave program that most new parents in the private sector do. Instead, many local school districts deduct the cost of a substitute teacher from educators' pay during parental leave.

phys-org.title: Getting outside despite your 9‑to‑5 job can improve your mental health
phys-org.description: The modern workday unfolds largely indoors. Long hours spent commuting, sitting in meetings and staring at screens can make time outdoors feel like a luxury. Finding time for nature in an already packed workday can feel impossible, especially if you think nature only "counts" when it involves hiking boots and camping gear.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s Energy Curse Is a Political Choice
proj-syn.description: It is no secret why African countries with large fossil-fuel reserves nonetheless have failed to reduce extreme poverty or provide reliable electricity to all households. Those in power have made a conscious choice to privilege hard-currency export revenues, some of which then finance elite consumption rather than public investment.

proj-syn.title: The EU’s Incredible Shrinking Banking Sector
proj-syn.description: At the start of the millennium, all five of the largest European banks had a higher market capitalization than the largest US bank. What explains the fact that a quarter-century later, the largest US bank has a higher capitalization than all five top EU banks combined, and how can European policymakers address this dramatic reversal?

proj-syn.title: AI Must Enlarge the Economy, Not Divide It
proj-syn.description: To unlock AI’s full economic potential, we must steer it toward expansion. That requires replacing incentives that favor capital over labor with those that reward augmentation and investment in human capability.

proj-syn.title: Silicon, Not Software, Will Decide the AI Race
proj-syn.description: The AI race is no longer just about building better models. As competition shifts from scientific discovery to deployment, success increasingly depends on computing power, advanced semiconductors, physical infrastructure, and markets large enough to justify the enormous investments they require.

proj-syn.title: The Limits of Asia’s Two Major Growth Models
proj-syn.description: Data from a period in which both China and India pursued deliberate industrial policies show that neither country's development route is accessible to other countries. At best, their experience can alert policymakers to structural limitations and coordination problems that will require their own homegrown solutions.

proj-syn.title: The World Needs Compassionate AI
proj-syn.description: With AI having become the frontline of an intense global competition for economic and geopolitical power, speed is rewarded, scale is celebrated, and market dominance is prized above all else. Under such conditions, we risk forgetting the most important question: Whom is this intelligence ultimately meant to serve?

proj-syn.title: Trump’s New Tariffs Are an Opportunity to Fight Back
proj-syn.description: Once again, President Donald Trump is subverting domestic and international law in an effort to seize a larger fraction of global value and supply chains, and harming the US economy in the process. The longer that businesses and other governments avoid standing up to him, the greater the disaster that awaits us all.

proj-syn.title: Explaining China’s Industrial Competitiveness
proj-syn.description: External headwinds have not weakened China’s manufacturing competitiveness. That is because the Chinese economy combines an unusually large manufacturing base, deep supply chains, fast engineering feedback loops, and cutthroat domestic competition to create global powerhouses.

proj-syn.title: When Politicians Ignore Economic Expertise
proj-syn.description: As politicians encroach on areas that require technical knowledge, the risk of costly policy mistakes increases. The failures of Narendra Modi and Donald Trump show that when it comes to economic policymaking, political acumen is no substitute for a deep understanding of incentives, markets, and institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Beijing Model Meets the Brussels Effect
proj-syn.description: As Europe races to rebuild its industrial base, China is focusing more on influencing international standards and governance frameworks. The two powers are converging because neither can hope to claim a dominant position in the global energy transition by relying wholly on its traditional strengths.

proj-syn.title: The Mexican Government’s Economic Spin
proj-syn.description: By cherry-picking 12 data points that supposedly contradict top ratings agencies’ assessment of Mexico’s economy and fiscal outlook, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum recently presented a just-so story that should convince no one. A glimpse of what her list excludes makes that clear.

proj-syn.title: The Middle-Income Health Trap
proj-syn.description: Many countries that graduate from low- to middle-income status soon find themselves stuck in the position of being too rich to qualify for aid, too poor to secure reliable market-based financing, and too indebted to expand public-health spending. But it doesn't have to be this way.

proj-syn.title: Europe Is Fiddling While Rome Burns
proj-syn.description: Focusing only on emergency planning, disaster response, and recovery after each climate catastrophe is no longer enough in Europe. Policymakers urgently need to start mapping Europe’s long-term future, which will require a fundamental overhaul of its infrastructure, energy system, and major economic sectors.

proj-syn.title: Saving Democracy Requires Taxing Extreme Wealth
proj-syn.description: If lawmakers are serious about addressing the threat that dynastic wealth poses to American democracy, they can draw on considerable research that has gone into designing a wealth tax that avoids the pitfalls of other countries’ attempts. With the appearance of the world’s first trillionaire, there is no time to waste.

proj-syn.title: The AI Threat to Financial Stability
proj-syn.description: In episodes like the railroad boom and the dot-com bubble, creditors and shareholders were wiped out, because investment in a genuinely transformative technology outpaced any plausible near-term return. With the US financial system and asset markets having become a one-way bet on AI, such an outcome today could be catastrophic.

proj-syn.title: South Korea Bets on Industrial Policy Again
proj-syn.description: With industrial policy back in fashion worldwide, the question is not whether governments should intervene (they already do), but how they should proceed when they do not know in advance what will work. The answer lies in directed improvisation: creating the conditions for experimentation where it counts.
